# Phase 1 results (auto-generated by src/compare.py)

Copied from the Colab run output on 2026-10-19. That run used a Tesla T4. Every encoder logged
`[cuda ok]`. Extraction took MOMENT 867 s, DINOv2 1578 s and Qwen 501 s. The full logs and JSON
files were written next to the cached embeddings (`results/emb/`, not committed).

## Test-set text statistics (computed locally from the same split)
- 4,000 test reports, of which only 2,225 are unique. 50.9% of test reports have an exact
  duplicate. The most common is "sinus rhythm. normal ecg." with 329 copies.
- Some reports are English, not German. Some carry trailing machine text ("… 4.46 unbestätigter
  bericht").
- If ties among identical reports were broken at random, the best possible exact-match text R@1
  would be about 55.6%. So instance-level TS↔TXT retrieval is partly ill-posed on PTB-XL.
  Label-level (zero-shot diagnostic) retrieval is the better text test.

**Reading:** lead II moves *further* from the paper, with even stronger text alignment. So the lead

## Label-level evaluation (src/label_eval.py; 5 PTB-XL diagnostic superclasses; 3 seeds; Colab T4)
Test records with at least one diagnostic superclass are used. "Label P@10" is the share of the
top-10 retrieved test reports whose record has the *same superclass set* as the query; chance is
0.223. "Zero-shot AUROC" uses class prototypes = mean projected embedding of single-superclass
train reports; it is the macro AUROC over the 5 classes.

| | Lead I | Lead II |
|---|---|---|
| TS→TXT label P@10 (chance 0.223) | 0.333 ± 0.002 | 0.372 ± 0.004 |
| IMG→TXT label P@10 | 0.318 ± 0.002 | 0.350 ± 0.006 |
| TS zero-shot AUROC (text prototypes) | 0.684 ± 0.003 | 0.726 ± 0.003 |
| IMG zero-shot AUROC | 0.668 ± 0.003 | 0.711 ± 0.006 |
| Untrained heads, TS zero-shot AUROC | 0.516 ± 0.064 | 0.522 ± 0.030 |
| Reference: supervised linear probe on frozen MOMENT features (AUROC) | 0.829 | 0.854 |

**Reading:** the aligned space carries real diagnostic meaning. Zero-shot AUROC is about 0.68–0.73
against 0.5 for untrained heads, and label P@10 is well above chance. It still sits well below
what the frozen MOMENT features support with supervision (0.83–0.85). Contrastive alignment to
reports recovers only part of the diagnostic information the encoder already has. That's a
concrete, measurable gap for the adaptation pilot to target. (Untrained-head label P@10 falls
below chance, 0.10 vs. 0.22, because random projections systematically favor non-matching
reports, so the chance column is the right floor for that metric.)

## Phase-2 pilot, seed 0, lead I (src/adapt.py; matched extra budget ≈295k params; Colab T4)
All arms train on the mean of 2 random windows per step and evaluate on all 10, so the head arm
differs slightly from phase 1 (TS–TXT margin 0.371 vs. 0.386). All three ran 50 epochs.
**This is one seed.**

| Arm | Extra params | Best val loss | TS–TXT margin ↑ | TS–TXT Procrustes ↓ | TS–TXT CKA ↑ | TS–TXT R@1 | TS–IMG R@1 | TS zero-shot AUROC | TS→TXT label P@10 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| head | 0 | 11.19 | 0.371 | 1.183 | 0.297 | 1.26% | 62.2% | 0.687 | 0.330 |
| deep_head (width 191) | 294,335 | 11.22 | 0.368 | 1.191 | 0.294 | 1.23% | 61.2% | 0.685 | 0.331 |
| **lora (r = 8, q/v, 12 layers)** | 294,912 | **11.02** | **0.388** | **1.159** | **0.311** | **1.51%** | **65.9%** | 0.684 | 0.339 |

IMG–TXT (no TS involved) is unchanged across arms (margin 0.370–0.374), as expected.

**Reading (single seed, so provisional):**
1. **Same budget, different place:** spending ~295k parameters on a deeper head does nothing, and
   is even slightly worse. Spending them as LoRA inside MOMENT improves every *geometric* TS
   metric: TS–TXT margin +0.017, Procrustes −0.024, CKA +0.014, TS–TXT R@1 +0.25 points, TS–IMG
   R@1 +3.7 points. That fits the hypothesis that the bottleneck is the encoder's geometry, not the
   readout.
2. **But diagnostic content doesn't move:** zero-shot AUROC stays at 0.684 vs. 0.687, and label
   P@10 rises only +0.009. The gap to the supervised probe (0.83) stays open. LoRA makes TS
   embeddings line up better with their *own* report and plot, but it doesn't make them more
   diagnostic. Better geometric alignment ≠ better downstream semantics. That's the question the
   paper itself raises, and the duplicate-heavy, indirect reports are a likely reason.
3. **Caveats:** one seed. In phase 1 the head-arm seed spread was ≤0.001 on margin, so +0.017 is
   probably real, but LoRA's own seed variance is unknown. A full LoRA run takes about 2.9 h on a
   T4. Lead I only, rank 8 only.

## Steps A + B: objective variants scored with fairer metrics (lead I, 3 seeds each, Colab T4)
`src/train_heads_v2.py` + `src/metrics_v2.py`, on the cached phase-1 embeddings (frozen encoders, heads
only). All variants use the same protocol and stop early on the *standard* InfoNCE val loss.
Means over seeds 0–2 (seed spread ≤ 0.002 on margin and AUROC). TS–TXT pair shown.

| Objective (text pairs) | Cos margin ↑ | Procrustes, paper ↓ | Procrustes, symmetric ↓ | R@1, paper rule | R@1, dup-aware | Zero-shot AUROC ↑ | Label P@10 ↑ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| infonce (paper) | 0.386 | 1.160 | 0.816 | 1.14% | 2.48% | 0.684 | 0.333 |
| dupmask (identical reports = positives) | 0.385 | 1.160 | 0.816 | 1.18% | 2.53% | 0.684 | 0.334 |
| soft (text-similarity soft targets) | 0.320 | 1.271 | 0.856 | 1.16% | 2.30% | **0.722** | 0.327 |
| label (diagnosis = positives; ORACLE, uses labels) | 0.210 | 1.492 | 0.910 | 0.55% | 1.32% | 0.724 | 0.313 |

"R@1, paper rule" = exact-index match with ties broken at random, as the paper's code effectively
does. The phase-1 numbers above counted exact ties as hits, which slightly favours TS→TXT; use this
column for comparisons with the paper.

**Reading:**
1. **The alignment metrics and diagnostic content move in opposite directions.** Moving down the
   table, every paper-style alignment metric gets *worse* (margin 0.386 → 0.210, Procrustes up,
   retrieval down), while zero-shot diagnosis gets *better* (0.684 → 0.72). Ranked by the paper's
   metrics, the most diagnostically useful models come last.
2. **Soft targets from the frozen text encoder reach the label oracle's diagnostic level
   (0.722 vs. 0.724) without using any labels**, while the paper's metrics call them worse than the
   baseline.
3. **Masking exact duplicates does nothing** (dupmask ≈ infonce on every metric). Identical reports
   already map to *identical* text embeddings, so the "false negative" is a symmetric tie the
   standard loss can't act on anyway. What helps is treating *similar but different* reports as
   related.
4. **Symmetric vs. paper Procrustes:** the symmetric version stays in [0, 1] (0.82–0.91 against
   1.16–1.49) and ranks these four objectives the same way. So in this comparison the scale issue
   distorts absolute values but doesn't flip the ordering. Critique #2 stays about interpretability,
   not about this ranking.
5. **Duplicate-aware retrieval roughly doubles R@1** (≈1.1% → ≈2.5%), quantifying how much of the
   paper-rule TS→TXT retrieval failure is ties among identical reports.

## Matched-budget pilot: all 3 seeds (lead I; Colab T4)
| Arm | Extra params | TS–TXT margin (s0 / s1 / s2) | TS–IMG R@1 (s0 / s1 / s2) | TS zero-shot AUROC (s0 / s1 / s2) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| head | 0 | 0.371 / 0.371 / 0.370 | 62.2 / 62.3 / 62.2 % | see results_adapt_head_leadI.json |
| deep_head | 294,335 | 0.368 / ~0.369 / 0.367 | 61.2 / 61.9 / 61.8 % | see JSON |
| **lora** | 294,912 | **0.388 / 0.388 / 0.388** | **65.9 / 63.8 / 65.4 %** | 0.684 / 0.680 / 0.684 |

**Confirmed over 3 seeds:** at a matched budget, LoRA inside MOMENT raises TS–TXT margin by +0.017
(head-arm seed spread ≤ 0.001) and TS–IMG R@1 by ~+3 points. The deeper head gives nothing. Zero-shot
diagnosis stays flat (0.683 vs. 0.684–0.687). Adapting the encoder improves geometric alignment, not
diagnostic content. That's the same dissociation as in Steps A + B.

## Sweep: 63 head-only models (lead I; Colab T4; `src/sweep.py`, `src/analyze_sweep.py`)
Grid: objective family {infonce, soft, label} × mix {.25,.5,.75,1} × soft-τ {.02,.05,.1,.2} × training τ
{0.07, 0.2, 0.5}. Each model has test alignment metrics, validation alignment metrics, zero-shot AUROC
(text prototypes), a linear-probe AUROC on the projected TS embedding, and patient-level 95% bootstrap
CIs (200 resamples). Full tables are in `results/sweep_analysis_leadI.md` on Drive.

**1. Probe AUROC is flat; zero-shot AUROC isn't.** The probe on projected embeddings is 0.823–0.833 for
every model (frozen-encoder reference 0.829; CI half-width ≈ 0.008). Zero-shot ranges from 0.672 to
0.807. The objectives change how *readable the diagnosis is through text*, not the diagnostic
information in the embedding.

**2. Alignment metrics anti-correlate with zero-shot AUROC.** Spearman ρ across models, with metrics
sign-flipped so + means "better alignment goes with better zero-shot":

| Metric | All 63 | Within τ = 0.07 | Within τ = 0.2 | Within τ = 0.5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cosine margin | −0.55 | −0.86 | −0.94 | −0.79 |
| Procrustes (paper) | −0.62 | −0.86 | −0.93 | −0.79 |
| Procrustes (symmetric) | −0.64 | −0.87 | −0.93 | −0.77 |
| RBF-CKA | −0.63 | −0.86 | −0.94 | −0.72 |
| Mutual kNN@5 | −0.68 | −0.84 | −0.73 | −0.17 |
| R@1, exact (paper rule) | −0.26 | −0.26 | −0.77 | −0.10 |
| **R@1, duplicate-aware** | **+0.19** | **+0.57** | −0.38 | +0.16 |

Exceptions exist (e.g. soft, mix 0.25, soft-τ 0.05, τ 0.07: margin 0.220 and zero-shot 0.672, below the
0.695 baseline). The negative trend still holds within each objective family (label family: ρ −0.73
to −0.83).

**3. Model-selection cost.** Pick the model with the best *validation* metric and report its *test*
zero-shot AUROC. The prespecified criterion (validation zero-shot AUROC) picks soft, mix 1.0,
soft-τ 0.2, τ 0.2: test 0.807 [0.798, 0.816].

| Selector (validation) | Model picked | Test zero-shot AUROC | Loss vs. criterion |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cosine margin / Procrustes (both) | infonce, τ 0.5 (the paper's objective) | 0.696 [0.687, 0.707] | **−0.111** |
| RBF-CKA | label, mix 0.25, τ 0.5 | 0.706 | −0.101 |
| Mutual kNN@5 | soft, mix 1.0, soft-τ 0.02, τ 0.2 | 0.685 | −0.123 |
| R@1, exact | label, mix 0.25, τ 0.07 | 0.712 | −0.095 |
| **R@1, duplicate-aware** | soft, mix 1.0, soft-τ 0.1, τ 0.07 | **0.802** | **−0.005** |

Within each training temperature the picture is the same: the standard metrics pick the infonce
baseline (loss 0.107–0.121), and duplicate-aware R@1 picks the best or near-best model (loss
0.000–0.041). Probe AUROC loss is ≤ 0.006 for every selector, which fits finding 1.

**Reading:** on PTB-XL, choosing a model by the paper's alignment metrics would cost about 0.11 AUROC
of zero-shot (text-queried) diagnostic discrimination, roughly 10× the patient-level CI half-width.
The cost is in text-based readout, not in the information the embedding carries. Duplicate-aware
retrieval, the one metric that doesn't penalize grouping reports with identical text, largely avoids
the cost.

replaced by its k-means centroid (fit on train), so the text gets less specific while the examples stay

| k = 500 | 466 | -0.91 | -0.91 | -0.94 | -0.45 | -0.60 | +0.38 |
| k = 100 | 100 | -0.95 | -0.95 | -0.94 | -0.27 | -0.76 | +0.29 |
| k = 20 | 20 | -0.75 | -0.75 | -0.60 | +0.47 | -0.74 | -0.83 |

Selection cost (test zero-shot AUROC lost when picking by the validation metric vs. by validation zero-shot AUROC):

| Text | margin | Procrustes | CKA | mKNN | R@1 exact | R@1 dup-aware |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| original | 0.121 | 0.121 | 0.121 | 0.123 | 0.106 | 0.000 |
| k = 500 | 0.072 | 0.072 | 0.072 | 0.070 | 0.056 | 0.000 |
| k = 100 | 0.052 | 0.052 | 0.052 | 0.043 | 0.040 | 0.003 |
| k = 20 | 0.021 | 0.021 | 0.021 | 0.000 | 0.016 | 0.014 |

| Text | InfoNCE zero-shot [95% CI] | Best zero-shot [95% CI] | Best model | Probe range | InfoNCE margin |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| original | 0.686 [0.676, 0.697] | 0.807 [0.798, 0.816] | soft mix 1, st 0.2 | 0.828-0.833 | 0.386 |
| k = 500 | 0.733 [0.724, 0.745] | 0.805 [0.796, 0.815] | soft mix 1, st 0.2 | 0.827-0.832 | 0.319 |
| k = 100 | 0.751 [0.740, 0.762] | 0.803 [0.794, 0.812] | soft mix 1, st 0.2 | 0.827-0.832 | 0.273 |
| k = 20 | 0.789 [0.779, 0.799] | 0.810 [0.802, 0.818] | label mix 1 | 0.827-0.831 | 0.195 |

**Reading:** the reversal is largest with the original, most specific text, and shrinks as the text
gets coarser. Plain InfoNCE improves steadily (0.686 -> 0.789) while the best model stays at ~0.81,
so the selection cost falls from 0.121 to 0.021. With instance-specific reports, InfoNCE pushes apart
signals whose reports differ in wording but not diagnosis. Coarse text removes those distinctions, so
instance alignment and class-level usefulness converge. The margin/Procrustes/CKA anti-correlation
persists within each condition (most models still trade margin for zero-shot), but its cost shrinks.

## Within-group information loss (lead I; 13 models at tau 0.2 per text condition; `src/info_loss.py`)
Groups = test ECGs sharing an identical report (original) or a k-means text cluster. Group spread =
mean within-group cosine distance / mean random-pair distance (higher = same-text ECGs less tightly
grouped relative to the whole space). wg_* = probe scores centered within groups (diagnosis: only on
groups whose members disagree on a superclass). Age and sex are absent from the reports.

| Text | Model | Zero-shot | Group spread | wg diagnosis AUROC | Age R² | wg age R² | Sex AUROC | wg sex AUROC |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| original | frozen encoder | - | 0.755 | 0.680 | 0.409 | 0.206 | 0.781 | 0.792 |
| original | InfoNCE | 0.686 | 0.868 | 0.679 | 0.406 | 0.195 | 0.769 | 0.775 |
| original | best (soft 1/0.2) | 0.807 | 0.946 | 0.678 | 0.387 | 0.174 | 0.760 | 0.766 |
| k = 500 | InfoNCE | 0.733 | 0.885 | 0.674 | 0.405 | 0.220 | 0.773 | 0.746 |
| k = 500 | best (soft 1/0.2) | 0.805 | 0.946 | 0.672 | 0.385 | 0.201 | 0.760 | 0.731 |
| k = 100 | InfoNCE | 0.751 | 0.900 | 0.668 | 0.405 | 0.255 | 0.773 | 0.751 |
| k = 100 | best (soft 1/0.2) | 0.803 | 0.947 | 0.665 | 0.384 | 0.234 | 0.759 | 0.739 |
| k = 20 | InfoNCE | 0.789 | 0.945 | 0.682 | 0.405 | 0.279 | 0.770 | 0.753 |
| k = 20 | best (label 1) | 0.810 | 0.965 | 0.683 | 0.393 | 0.269 | 0.760 | 0.743 |

Spearman across the 13 models, each measure vs zero-shot AUROC:

| Text | Group spread | wg diagnosis | Age R² | wg age R² | Sex AUROC | wg sex AUROC |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| original | +0.90 | -0.24 | -0.84 | -0.69 | -0.19 | -0.75 |
| k = 500 | +0.83 | -0.74 | -0.84 | -0.86 | -0.84 | -0.88 |
| k = 100 | +0.91 | -0.53 | -0.95 | -0.92 | -0.93 | -0.94 |
| k = 20 | +0.82 | +0.51 | -0.80 | -0.77 | -0.73 | -0.75 |

Margin vs zero-shot (Spearman): raw, and rank-partial given group spread / age R² / wg sex AUROC:
original -0.91 / -0.46 / -0.72 / -0.79; k500 -0.91 / -0.77 / -0.67 / -0.49; k100 -0.95 / -0.65 / -0.21 / -0.53;
k20 -0.75 / +0.41 / +0.11 / -0.12. Group spread vs margin: rho -0.97 to -0.99 in every condition (nearly
collinear, so the partials are poorly conditioned).

**Reading:** in every condition, models with better zero-shot AUROC keep slightly less of the
information the text doesn't carry (age and sex, globally and within groups; rho -0.7 to -0.95), and
their same-text groups are less tightly separated. The absolute changes are small (age R² 0.406 ->
0.387, sex AUROC 0.769 -> 0.760, within-group age R² 0.195 -> 0.174), and within-group diagnosis is
unchanged (0.665-0.683 everywhere). So the high-alignment models are not "more informative" in any
diagnostic sense; they retain a little more text-irrelevant signal detail and finer text-specific
grouping, which the alignment metrics reward and class-level use does not need. n = 13 per
condition; no CIs on the preservation measures yet.

## Cleanup checks (13 tau-0.2 models, original reports; `src/cleanup.py`; Colab T4)
Label-free prompts: `src/prompts_superclass.json`, frozen (committed) before evaluation; pre-registered
readout = ensemble of 8 prompts per class (4 English, 4 German). Corrections are fit on TRAIN
embeddings only and applied to the head outputs before L2 normalization. "unsup 9" = InfoNCE + 8
soft-target models (no label-target arms).

Test AUROC, InfoNCE vs best model, and Spearman (margin vs AUROC) across models:

| Readout | Correction | Models | InfoNCE | Best | Gap | rho margin | rho R@1 dup-aware |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| report prototypes | none | unsup 9 | .686 | .807 | .121 | -0.88 | +0.14 |
| report prototypes | text-side centering | unsup 9 | .789 | .809 | .019 | -0.73 | +0.36 |
| report prototypes | shared centering | all 13 | .757 | .806 | .049 | | |
| label-free prompts | none | unsup 9 | .571 | .760 | .189 | -0.95 | +0.18 |
| label-free prompts | text-side centering | unsup 9 | .681 | .753 | .072 | -0.55 | +0.49 |
| label-free prompts | shared centering | all 13 | .646 | .750 | .104 | | |

Signal-side centering alone changes nothing (a per-class constant shift). Whitening (ZCA, shrinkage 0.1,
fit on train) lowers every model and reverses the ordering; not diagnostic (it amplifies low-variance
directions). Best model in every unsupervised row: soft, mix 1.0, soft-tau 0.2.

Sweep correlations without the label-target arms (51 of 63 models): margin -0.53, symmetric Procrustes
-0.63, CKA -0.64, mutual kNN -0.67, R@1 exact -0.30, R@1 dup-aware +0.29; within training temperature,
margin -0.83 / -0.93 / -0.74 (tau .07 / .2 / .5). Selection cost by validation margin: .107-.121 within
each temperature; by dup-aware R@1: .000.

AUROC minus the full-labeled-validation pick's, same test resample; 95% interval; selection frequency):

| report prototypes | val mutual kNN | .690 | -.116 [-.132, -.081] | InfoNCE (.47) |

| report prototypes | val labels, all | .806 | 0 | soft 1/.2 (1.0) |

The best soft model is also the one picked by validation (labels: 100% of resamples), so it is not a
test-set pick. Not yet run: the selection test on the text-centered readouts. Duplicate-aware chance
levels (random ranking), test: R@1 .0142, R@10 .109 (exact R@1 chance .00025).

**Reading:** a large part of the report-prototype gap is text-side prototype geometry (a shared mean
direction in the projected report embeddings): text-side centering lifts InfoNCE from .686 to .789 and
leaves a .019 gap. With the label-free prompts a .072 gap survives the same correction. Selecting by
validation margin/Procrustes/CKA picks InfoNCE almost always and costs .12 (reports) to .19 (prompts)
AUROC under the uncorrected readouts; duplicate-aware retrieval and a 25-patient labeled validation set
both come within .01.
